title.narrative: ROAF/Central Sahel/Inclusive, Safe, Resilient and Sustainable Human Settlements in the Sahel – A regional approach to build community resilience across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace nexus

description.narrative:
UN-Habitat and UNDP have developed this 15-month initiative to promote a regional resilience-based approach with the aim of reducing the gap between humanitarian needs and available resources for risk-informed and sustainable development of urban areas in the Sahel, rather than merely responding and managing the disasters and crises in cities and towns when they occur. It aims to support evidence-based decision making, through a spatial/territorial approach, at the regional, national and local levels to ultimately increase the resilience of urban communities, to both manage and leverage the spatial transformations in the region for the achievement of sustainable and resilient, risk-informed development and sustainable livelihoods for all, including the youth, women, internally displaced populations, refugees, and other marginalised groups.
Through a forward-looking analysis, the Project will adopt an integrated territorial approach at the different scales (regional, national, local) to enhance the understanding of ongoing transformations in the region and better inform policy and programmatic interventions by humanitarian, development and peace actors. Guided by data on urbanisation and other factors that shape resilience of communities and settlements in the Sahel, this initiative intends to promote joint decision-making and cooperation across the HDP nexus actors for strategic and solution-oriented investments, leading to more inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable human settlements in the region. The expected outcome is to provide a solid basis for transforming urban areas in the Sahel (or its system of cities) into powerhouses for local socio-economic development, with robust urban risk management systems to respond and adapt to the increasing climatic and disaster risks and other shocks exacerbated by conflicts, based on human rights and gender equality principles, leaving no one and no place behind.
Therefore, the Project is also meant to strengthen capacities of regional, national and local institutions and stakeholders, including urban local government bodies and municipal authorities, in sustainable urbanisation and urban risk management. This implies that local institutions have adequate organizational capacities, as well as resources and plans in place to prevent, prepare for and recover from crises. For this purpose, the project seeks to reach the following Expected Accomplishments:
EA1. A better understanding of the territorial dynamics at the different scales in the Sahel region has been reached among humanitarian, development and peace actors. EA2. Local leaders and communities of the Sahel are better equipped to progressively enhance the resilience of their city/town to shocks and stresses. Through an evidence-based and consultative approach, a Regional Assessment of the System of Cities of the Sahel region will be prepared, with key/actionable recommendations at the different scales (regional, national and local) to promote inclusion, safety, resilience and sustainability of the human settlements of the region. It will be presented in the form of an atlas including illustrative maps and key/actionable recommendations, which can support decision-making in terms of major interventions/investments at regional level and inform country priorities. Different themes will be analysed:
1. Risk Analysis at the regional level: 2. Spatial Analysis at the regional level 3. Governance Analysis at the national level 4. Resilience Analysis at the local level
Finally, the project will allow local and national authorities to build their capacities in resilient city planning through the implementation of the CityRAP tool, and to derive their City Framework for Actions (RFAs). An online workshop is planned to be diffused through the region to disseminate the acquired knowledge.
